markdown_report:
Propose a bounded calibration suite for the existing temporal diagnostic adapter before adding further perturbations. At 10% progress, establishing that probes detect known behavioral changes is a feasible next step; no validation improvement is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, recent-history deletion changes scores more than oldest-history deletion in the supplied earlier checkpoint. Compaction also changes positions, so this supports sensitivity rather than causal recency claims. Second, unchanged-history repetition passed across all four datasets. This verifies repeatability but cannot establish that intervention labels describe what the probes measure. Third, the latest supplied Industrial and Electronics negative-margin fractions are 24.61% and 27.97%. These training-panel observations motivate investigation but cannot rank models by validation quality.

**Insights from related work.** Metamorphic testing evaluates relations between executions when exact labels are unavailable [1]. It motivates controlled diagnostic backends with analytically known invariances. Counterfactual faithfulness research separates plausible explanations from prediction dependence [2]. Consequently, textual agreement should remain separate from measured model sensitivity. Sampled-ranking research demonstrates that sampled metrics can misrepresent full-catalog comparisons [3]. Calibration success therefore cannot substitute for the pinned validation objective.

These insights define three directions: execution correctness, behavioral sensitivity, and predictive usefulness. The framework below separates their evidence:

| Layer | Controlled relation | Supported conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Scoring interface | Candidate permutation reorders scores | Candidate alignment |
| Earlier-history probe | Latest-item-only backend ignores earlier edits | Probe specificity |
| History-independent control | Frequency backend ignores every history edit | Control correctness |
| Host validation | Unchanged pinned protocol | Selection quality |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores denote originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Calibrate temporal probes with controlled backends [1,2] | 5/7/4 | Originality: useful integration; established relations. Potential: reusable audit; accuracy link unproven. Difficulty: existing hooks suffice; careful alignment required. |
| Add frequency-matched candidate stress tests [3] | 4/6/5 | Originality: task-specific combination; standard sampling. Potential: reveals candidate dependence; false negatives remain. Difficulty: training counts suffice; pool accounting expands scope. |
| Test a recency-weighted residual scorer | 4/7/6 | Originality: diagnostic-motivated combination; established pooling. Potential: directly tests ranking gains; recency may reinforce shortcuts. Difficulty: small branch; predictor and training must change together. |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze one compact training-only panel and reuse identical prefixes, targets, candidates, and perturbations. Run the actual trained model plus diagnostic-only latest-item and training-frequency backends. Require candidate-permutation equivariance, earlier-edit invariance for the latest-item backend, and all-edit invariance for the frequency backend. Record numerical residuals, counts, intervention strength, and failures separately from empirical trained-model effects.

Preserve both diagnostic entry points, isolated randomness, model modes, four-category routing, and unavailable-data semantics. Use fixed floating-point tolerances and a recorded computation cap. Leave deployment scoring unchanged; selection remains host macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Calibrate the paired temporal diagnostic adapter using a small set of analytically checkable scoring relations. Evaluate the actual trained model through its existing hooks, and run the same diagnostic transformations against explicitly labeled latest-item-only and training-frequency control backends. Separate interface failures, control failures, and empirical trained-model sensitivity.
idea.motivation: The supplied unchanged-history checks establish repeatability, while positional controls and the prospective sensitivity–accuracy pilot remain unavailable. More perturbations would increase diagnostic breadth without establishing measurement specificity. At early research progress, bounded controls can reveal candidate misalignment, accidental latest-item edits, or history-dependent control implementations before further search budget is spent. Qualitative feedback remains hypothesis-generating because ownership, compatibility, satisfaction, and simulator traits are unobserved.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions. The actual-model branch must use view.model and architecture-compatible log2feats/predict_score; never replace view.model with a control or describe control outputs as trained-model predictions.

Reuse an independently constructed persisted training-history panel without iterating the active loader. Cap calibration at 64 eligible users per category and three persisted perturbation draws, declared before execution. Keep final training targets and fixed diagnostic candidate IDs identical across conditions. These remain in-sample observations. Record category name, checkpoint identity, item-map fingerprint, exact control definitions, panel fingerprint, candidate IDs, eligible counts, and runtime.

Define the latest-item control explicitly as s(h,i)=dot(E[last_nonpadding(h)],E[i]), using detached trained item embeddings and the original scoring scale without learned sequence features. It is a deliberately simplified scoring backend. Earlier-item substitution and permutation must preserve the latest item and nonempty history. Latest-item deletion is outside this invariant. Define the frequency control as s(h,i)=log1p(c_i), where c_i counts public training interactions within the routed category. It must ignore history entirely. Neither control is a newly trained reference model or evidence of predictive usefulness.

For each backend, permute candidate columns and invert the permutation before comparing scores. Require per-candidate score agreement rather than only equal margins. Repeated candidates, if permitted by an interface, must retain their column identity; the diagnostic panel should use unique candidate IDs. Exclude empty histories from the latest-item condition and report them explicitly. Use float32 comparisons with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, recording dtype, maximum absolute residual, maximum scaled residual, nonfinite counts, and failure counts. Apply invariance requirements only where their premises hold. Do not require the actual trained model to change under perturbations: zero sensitivity is a possible measured result.

Verify calibration sensitivity with a deterministic diagnostic-only misalignment injection: reverse score columns without reversing candidate IDs on a synthetic distinct-score fixture. The alignment check must fail for that fixture and pass for its correct counterpart. Report this as detection of one injected mapping error, not a general fault-detection rate. Keep synthetic fixtures separate from recommendation-quality measurements.

Preserve heterogeneous model modes, global and accessible explicit-generator states, and registered buffers using try/finally. Restore and report unexpected buffer mutation. Do not claim subsequent optimizer-step equivalence unless independently measured. Aggregate actual-model effects within users and then categories; macro summaries require all four datasets. Report invariant failures by category rather than hiding them in a macro mean. An invariant failure invalidates the affected diagnostic comparison, not automatically the model checkpoint or host validation result.

Retain the native twenty-user recommendation requirement: five real training users per category receive full-catalog, training-unseen recommendations through the actual trained scorer, using chunked catalog scoring. These lists are qualitative and remain separate from calibration fixtures and sampled panels. Do not infer item categories, ownership, compatibility, ratings, reviews, prices, stores, or latent simulator traits.

Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, single-GPU execution, and trial-local artifacts. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS=200 as the host environment default. This diagnostic-only proposal changes neither architecture nor production inference, so no predictor change is necessary. Charge calibration and diagnostic computation to the shared GPU budget. The host's pinned macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection criterion; no training or validation gain is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Compatibility argument retained; active loader is never consumed.
        panel = load_fixed_training_panel(max_users=64, draws=3, seed=42)
        state = capture_modes_rng_and_buffers(self.view.model)
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                trained = ActualModelBackend(self.view)
                latest = LastItemDotBackend(self.view.item_emb)
                frequency = TrainingFrequencyBackend(self.view.user_train)
                for batch in panel:
                    candidates = batch.fixed_candidates
                    for backend in (trained, latest, frequency):
                        scores = backend.score(batch.prefix, candidates)
                        permutation = batch.persisted_candidate_permutation
                        permuted = backend.score(
                            batch.prefix, candidates[:, permutation])
                        record_score_equivariance(
                            scores, permuted[:, inverse(permutation)],
                            atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)

                    for variant in batch.persisted_variants:
                        record_actual_model_effect(trained, batch, variant)
                        if variant.preserves_latest_item:
                            require_paired_score_invariance(
                                latest, batch, variant, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)
                        require_paired_score_invariance(
                            frequency, batch, variant, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)

                record_synthetic_alignment_check_and_injected_failure()
                record_five_training_users_full_catalog_lists(trained)
                return {
                    'metrics': summarize_with_counts_and_failure_scope(),
                    'metric_definitions': formulas_premises_limits_and_runtime()
                }
        finally:
            restore_and_check_state(self.view.model, state)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return render_grounded_prompt(
        metrics=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        distinguish_controls_from_trained_predictions=True,
        distinguish_invariant_failure_from_empirical_sensitivity=True,
        forbid_accuracy_causality_and_unobserved_trait_claims=True)

# Pseudocode: helpers require integration with the existing architecture adapter.
# No training, validation query, or production predictor mutation occurs here.

originality.positive: Connects known invariances, diagnostic scoring controls, and explicit failure attribution within the existing temporal adapter.
originality.negative: Metamorphic relations and simplified control scorers are established; the contribution is their task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides reusable checks as scoring architectures and temporal probes evolve, with bounded computation and clear failure conditions.
future_potential.negative: Correct diagnostics may still offer little guidance for improving pinned validation HR@10; calibration does not establish that relationship.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses persisted panels and embedding/scoring hooks without retraining or altering production inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Candidate alignment, architecture-compatible scoring, state restoration, and faithful failure reporting still require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] An empirical study on metamorphic testing for recommender systems
contributions: Studies recommender reliability through relations between executions when exact expected recommendations are unavailable.
Motivates explicit invariance checks and controlled error injections.
limitations: The supplied account does not establish a validated temporal fault-signature suite for SASRec.
Passing metamorphic checks does not demonstrate recommendation accuracy.

related_work.title: [2] Walk the Talk? LLM faithfulness
contributions: Uses counterfactual interventions to examine whether cited explanatory concepts influence predictions.
Motivates separating textual plausibility from measured model dependence.
limitations: Does not directly validate the proposed SASRec diagnostic controls.
Prediction sensitivity alone does not identify causal user preferences.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can misrepresent full-catalog comparisons.
Supports keeping sampled training-panel diagnostics distinct from benchmark selection.
limitations: Does not prescribe the proposed calibration suite.
Its sampling critique does not authorize changing the task's pinned evaluator.
